title: Visual Perception for Robotics Supporting Few-Shot Learning
venue: PhD thesis, Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, 2026

glance.application: Robots that must handle new objects at short notice: retrieving tools, sorting batteries, collecting litter, finding hazardous items.
glance.challenge: Fully supervised deep learning needs large datasets, compute, preparation time and ML expertise that real robot deployments rarely have.
glance.solution: Build on pretrained vision backbones and adapt them from a few examples with prototypes and lightweight add-on modules. Interactive teaching lets operators steer what the model looks at.
glance.benefit: Practical perception systems with minimal task-specific training. Human interaction resolves ambiguity when data is scarce, which helps most with very similar categories.

title: Interactive Fine-grained Few-shot Detection of Tools
authors: P. Keller, L. Strecker, F. Durchdewald, F. Graaf, T. Schnell, R. Dillmann
venue: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS), 2025

glance.application: Mobile robots that find and fetch specific household and industrial tools.
glance.challenge: Tools are rare, look very alike and are missing from large datasets. The target classes also change from mission to mission.
glance.solution: DE-fine-ViT extends the DE-ViT detector with class and part prototypes that the user builds interactively, plus a re-evaluation module that uses the parts to separate look-alike classes. No fine-tuning.
glance.benefit: A detector for look-alike tools that adapts to new classes without retraining, plus a new fine-grained power-drill dataset. Over DE-ViT, mAP@50:95 rises from 0.46 to 0.70 on a mini tool set and from 0.25 to 0.40 on the power drills. Fine-tuned detectors still score higher but must be retrained after every class change.

title: Towards a Versatile Teleoperation System for Mobile Robots through a Modular Architecture and Scalable Autonomy
authors: S. Bellmann, T. Trapp, E. Hofele, D. Oberacker, M. Grosse Besselmann, N. Spielbauer, P. Keller, L. Puck, T. Schnell, R. Dillmann, A. Roennau

glance.application: Mobile manipulators doing maintenance tasks in factories under remote control.
glance.challenge: Full autonomy fails in unforeseen situations. Pure teleoperation is repetitive and requires close familiarity with the robot's interface.
glance.solution: A modular framework with scalable autonomy: manual control with a 3D mouse, adaptable through modes and restrictions, combined with automated subroutines.
glance.benefit: Shows how scalable autonomy can support the operator instead of competing with them: subroutines take over repetitive steps. Two maintenance-inspired scenarios explore how this eases operation, especially for novice users.

title: Low-Compute Trash Segmentation Using Pretrained Vision Transformers Without Fine-Tuning
authors: P. Keller, M. Möck, G. Heppner, R. Dillmann
venue: International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Applications (ICARA), 2025

glance.application: Autonomous robots that collect litter outdoors.
glance.challenge: Litter is so diverse that no dataset covers every item, and trained detectors miss kinds of waste they have not seen.
glance.solution: Use the attention maps of a frozen, pretrained vision transformer to locate and coarsely segment trash, with an LRP-based distraction branch to look away from common non-trash objects such as small animals.
glance.benefit: Trash segmentation with no trash-specific training and little compute. On kinds of litter missing from the training data, it holds up better than a trained Mask R-CNN, which stays more precise on the classes it was trained on.

title: Online Vision-Based 3D Reconstruction for Shared Human-Robot Workspaces
authors: P. Keller, G. Perez Rivera, T. Schnell, R. Dillmann
venue: International Conference on Electrical, Computer, Communications and Mechatronics Engineering (ICECCME), 2024

glance.application: Collision avoidance for robot arms in workspaces shared with people.
glance.challenge: People can put unknown obstacles such as boxes or tools anywhere at any time. The Lidar and depth sensors usually used to detect them are expensive.
glance.solution: Watch the workspace with calibrated, inexpensive RGB cameras. A hybrid of learned feature matching and classical image processing reconstructs obstacles online as simplified collision objects.
glance.benefit: Collision checking from plain RGB cameras, so no depth sensor is needed. It also captures weakly textured objects and surfaces, and runs in near real time with three cameras.

title: Interactive Teaching for Fine-Granular Few-Shot Object Recognition Using Vision Transformers
authors: P. Keller, D. Jost, A. Roennau, R. Dillmann
venue: IEEE International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP), 2024

glance.application: Teaching robots to recognize new, very similar objects from a handful of images.
glance.challenge: With few examples, a model can latch onto the wrong features. Interpretability shows this, but the user cannot correct it.
glance.solution: Part-based inference on pretrained vision transformers, plus a visual concept bank that translates features between human and model, so users can adjust what the model focuses on.
glance.benefit: Closes the feedback loop: users can correct what the model focuses on, which makes fine-grained recognition more robust and adapts the model quickly without fine-tuning. Even without interaction, accuracy is on par with the state of the art.

title: Robotic Sorting of Batteries Using Visual Few-shot Learning and Fusion with Depth Data
authors: P. Keller, J. Mangler, N. Hügel, M. Grosse Besselmann, A. Roennau, R. Dillmann
venue: International Conference on Electrical, Computer, Communications and Mechatronics Engineering (ICECCME), 2023

glance.application: Automated pre-sorting of used batteries on a conveyor belt so their materials can be recovered.
glance.challenge: Sorting by hand exposes workers to toxic substances, and there are no large training datasets of battery types.
glance.solution: Few-shot visual detection on an RGB camera, checked against depth data from a line scanner using expert rules on each battery type's dimensions.
glance.benefit: An automated sorting line that works with few training samples. Where most other approaches rely on one sensor, fusing in depth fixed the typical mix-ups: AAA batteries 20 % → 100 % and camera batteries 0 % → 100 % correctly sorted in the test run.

title: Intuitive Access to Versatile Assistive Services Provided by Agile Walking Robots Using Open Source LLMs
authors: P. Keller, B. Weng, R. Wilbrandt, F. Graaf, A. Roennau, R. Dillmann
venue: IROS Workshop on Assistive Robotics for Citizens, 2023

glance.domain: Natural-language robot control with large language models.
glance.application: Assistive services at home with a walking robot that has an arm (Spot).
glance.challenge: Assistive services need complex software architectures, and commanding a robot still takes programming expertise.
glance.solution: A prompt composer combines the user's request with known places, detected objects and documented skills. A local open-source LLM picks the next behavior-tree skill, and expressive error messages feed back into the next prompt.
glance.benefit: A concept that lets anyone command assistive services in plain language, built from combinable generic skills. Unlike similar approaches, it grounds requests in maps and detections, learns from error feedback, and runs locally with open-source LLMs for privacy.

title: ROBDEKON – Teilvorhaben: Autonome, mobile Roboter für die Dekontamination in schwierigen Umgebungen
titleEn: ROBDEKON subproject: autonomous mobile robots for decontamination in difficult environments
authors: J. Mangler, M. Große-Besselmann, P. Keller, N. Hügel, A. Roennau
venue: Final report (in German), FZI, 2023. Programme “Forschung für zivile Sicherheit”.

glance.domain: Robotics for civil security and decontamination.
glance.application: Robots that work in contaminated or hostile sites so that people do not have to.
glance.challenge: Contaminated sites endanger workers. Robots there must map unknown terrain, recognize hazards from little training data, and stay easy to operate.
glance.solution: FZI's part of ROBDEKON phase I: robot assistance functions developed with users, including 3D mapping, few-shot hazard detection, shared-control grasping, and a sorting cell for explosion-prone batteries.
glance.benefit: The final report bundles the subproject's results, from multi-robot field missions to the battery-sorting demonstrator, as a basis for the ROBDEKON II pilot scenarios.

title: Grasping and Retrieving Unknown Hazardous Objects with a Mobile Manipulator
authors: A. Roennau, J. Mangler, P. Keller, M. Grosse Besselmann, N. Hügel, R. Dillmann

glance.application: Finding and retrieving unknown hazardous objects, for example in decontamination missions.
glance.challenge: Dangerous, unknown objects have to be found and handled in difficult terrain without putting the operator at risk.
glance.solution: Shared operation to identify and localize the objects, 3D mapping of the site, and force-based shared-control grasping, backed by intuitive visualizations at several levels of abstraction.
glance.benefit: Operators can retrieve unknown hazards remotely and safely, combining the robot’s reliability with their own expertise. Evaluated successfully in a field test with two different mobile robots.

title: Embedded AI-Box for Visual Detection and Inspection with Mobile Robots in ROS2
authors: A. Tanev, J. C. Vasquez Tieck, G. Heppner, P. Keller, A. Roennau, R. Dillmann
venue: World Congress on Software Engineering (WCSE), Spring Event, 2022

glance.application: Giving mobile robots such as Spot onboard object and person detection.
glance.challenge: Deep-learning vision models need computing power and energy that mobile robots and embedded systems lack.
glance.solution: A plug-on AI-Box with dedicated deep-learning hardware, a camera, ROS 2 and Detectron2. Models are trained offline, then pruned and quantized to run on the box.
glance.benefit: Mobile robots get deep-learning vision without computing hardware of their own: the box installs easily, runs compressed models onboard, and extends to classification and segmentation.

title: Performance Evaluation of Real-Time ROS2 Robotic Control in a Time-Synchronized Distributed Network
authors: L. Puck, P. Keller, T. Schnell, C. Plasberg, A. Tanev, G. Heppner, A. Roennau, R. Dillmann
venue: IEEE International Conference on Automation Science and Engineering (CASE), 2021

glance.application: Robot controllers assembled from open ROS 2 components instead of manufacturers' black boxes.
glance.challenge: ROS 1 lacks real-time communication. Whether ROS 2 on DDS really delivers reliable latency and jitter was unclear.
glance.solution: Measure how ROS 2 messages are allocated and sent, on one host and across time-synchronized hosts, in an application from object detection to EtherCAT control. An oscilloscope validates the measurements externally.
glance.benefit: Externally validated latency and jitter figures, and evidence that ROS 2 reaches real-time capability with real-time-safe memory allocation and highly privileged processes.

title: Distributed and Synchronized Setup towards Real-Time Robotic Control using ROS2 on Linux
authors: L. Puck, P. Keller, T. Schnell, C. Plasberg, A. Tanev, G. Heppner, A. Roennau, R. Dillmann
venue: IEEE International Conference on Automation Science and Engineering (CASE), 2020

glance.application: Modular robot control where sensors, actuators and controllers are interchangeable.
glance.challenge: Industrial robots run monolithic black-box controllers whose components can be neither accessed nor exchanged.
glance.solution: A distributed, clock-synchronized real-time Linux setup for ROS 2, analyzed with system-inherent tools and non-invasive measurements.
glance.benefit: Comprehensive insights that guide ROS 2 applications on distributed, synchronized real-time Linux systems, a step from black-box controllers towards open, modular control.

title: Microsaccades for Neuromorphic Stereo Vision
authors: J. Kaiser, J. Weinland, P. Keller, L. Steffen, J. C. Vasquez Tieck, D. Reichard, A. Roennau, J. Conradt, R. Dillmann
venue: International Conference on Artificial Neural Networks (ICANN), 2018

glance.domain: Neuromorphic vision and stereo depth perception.
glance.application: Depth perception for biologically inspired robots.
glance.challenge: Event cameras report only changes in light, so they see nothing in a static scene, and stereo matching on them fails there.
glance.solution: A robotic head with two Dynamic Vision Sensors makes small microsaccade-like eye movements. Precise spike timing then helps match points between the two eyes.
glance.benefit: Disparities from static as well as dynamic scenes, showing that event sensors and active perception complement each other.
